thread:
oliver: heads-up: since ~09:12 we're seeing controller-manager leader elections flip every ~18s in us-east1. CPU looks fine but GPU attach jobs are failing with AttachVolume timeouts. pod create failures spiking, apiserver 5xx creeping up.
amanda: oncall here. can you paste leader election logs? `kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/controller-manager | tail -n 80`
oliver: paste: `I0316 09:12:04 election.go:239] observed leader change: old=oliver new=amanda` repeated ~30x. also cloud-controller-manager: `AttachVolume error: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded` in the same window.
raj: fyi i noticed a concurrent spike in node egress connections after the kernel roll; could be NAT ephemeral port pressure causing short stalls. packet fragmentation? not sure. `ip link show` looks normal though.
maria: confirmed from VPC metrics: NAT ephemeral ports hit ~94% between 09:10-09:25 in us-east1. lots of small outbound connections from image/model pulls during GPU init. if egress ports starve, kubelet and controller-manager RPCs can stall.
oliver: that matches behavior — many GPU init hooks do parallel `curl` calls to model-store. when NAT exhausted, lease renewals time out -> leader flips -> controller-manager restarts watchers -> more churn. :grimacing:
amanda: temp mitigations: (1) scale NAT capacity for the zone, (2) enable TCP port reuse on init scripts, (3) increase controller-manager `--leader-elect-lease-duration` from 15s -> 45s as a canary. i'll push the lease change to staging first.
raj: also consider throttling concurrent pulls during startup or a simple token-bucket around registry access. `--watch-cache` tweaks could help but risky under load.
maria: @amanda i can run `gcloud compute routers nats update ... --min-ports-per-vm` and patch the init to set `SO_REUSEPORT` for curl wrappers. i'll open a quick config PR.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary patch applied to controller-manager in staging at 09:46. monitoring: apiserver 5xx dropped from 3.4% -> 0.9% over 10m.
amanda: NAT scale rolled at 09:50, attach errors are dropping now. keeping the lease-duration change in canary for 1h. note: NAT capacity increase will add ~$1.2k/mo in us-east1 during peak — tagging cost impact.
oliver: tl;dr: root cause = ephemeral port exhaustion during bulk GPU job startups -> controlplane lease/renew timeouts -> leader election thrash -> attach failures. next actions: 1) backoff/retry in gpu init, 2) rate-limit model pulls, 3) introduce a central model cache, 4) update runbook.
maria: i'll add a "gpu-burst" runbook entry and a Grafana alert for NAT ephemeral port usage >80% and controller-manager leader flips >3/min. :white_check_mark:
raj: closing loop: i'll open the PR for socket reuse + model cache and link runbook edits. anyone want the postmortem template?
amanda: yes pls include timeline + cost delta and mitigations. i'll start the postmortem draft after we stabilize.
